## Purpose
The Mistral model catalog. It is read live from `GET /v1/models`, cached in `backend/model_catalog.json`, used to check every configured model (deprecated, retired, unknown or lacking a capability) and, optionally, to switch deprecated models to their replacement automatically.

## Responsibilities
- **`_path()`** returns `MODEL_CATALOG_PATH`, else `backend/model_catalog.json`.
- **`_normalise(card)`** keeps id, name, description, type (default "base"), owned_by, created, max_context_length, aliases, deprecation, deprecation_replacement_model, default_model_temperature, and the boolean `capabilities`.
- **`load()`** returns the cached catalog, or `{"fetched_at": None, "source": None, "models": [], "error": None}`.
- **`_save()`** writes atomically (a tmp file, then `os.replace`).
- **`index()`** maps every id and every alias to its card.
- **`model_status(model, capability)`** returns one of:
  - `unchecked` when the catalog is empty;
  - `unknown`: "'<m>' is not in the Mistral model list for this account";
  - `deprecated` or `retired`, chosen by whether the deprecation date has passed, with the replacement named;
  - `incapable`, when the capability flag is missing. Capabilities map to flags: chat to completion_chat, plus function_calling, moderation, ocr, vision and reasoning;
  - `ok`.
- **`fetch()`** needs `MISTRAL_API_KEY`. It calls `{MISTRAL_API_BASE_URL}/v1/models` with a 30 s timeout and raises on any status other than 200.
- **`refresh()`:**
  - holds an asyncio lock;
  - on a failure it saves the old catalog with `error` and `error_at` set, then re-raises;
  - otherwise it saves the new catalog and runs `review(apply=AUTO_UPGRADE_DEPRECATED_MODELS)`;
  - it adds `added` and `removed` ids compared with the previous catalog.
- **`review(apply)`:**
  - checks every backend setting of type `model` or `model_list`;
  - checks every Tool Service model setting, read through `tool_service.get_settings()`;
  - collects the issues;
  - with `apply`, updates single-model settings to their replacement in the backend store and the Tool Service.
- **`is_stale()`** is true when the catalog has never been fetched or is older than `MODEL_CATALOG_REFRESH_HOURS`. A value of 0 or less means never stale.
- **`refresh_loop()`** refreshes when the catalog is stale, then sleeps 3600 s, forever. A cancellation propagates.

## Key elements
See Responsibilities.

## Control flow
`main.lifespan` starts `refresh_loop`. The Settings routes call `refresh` and `review` on demand.

## Data, state and side effects
- Writes `model_catalog.json`.
- May change settings in the backend store and in the Tool Service.

## Configuration
`MISTRAL_API_KEY`, `MISTRAL_API_BASE_URL`, `MODEL_CATALOG_REFRESH_HOURS`, `AUTO_UPGRADE_DEPRECATED_MODELS` and `MODEL_CATALOG_PATH`.

## Interactions
- Used by `routes/settings.py`, by `core/decision.reasoning_capable` (which reads the cached file) and by `health._model_catalog`.

## Error handling and edge cases
- If the Tool Service is unreachable during a review, it is skipped with an info log.
- An upgrade that fails in the Tool Service is dropped from the `upgraded` list.

## Nuances and gotchas
- **Model lists are only flagged, never upgraded automatically.**
- **The catalog is fetched with the platform key**, so it lists what the Default workspace's account can call.

## How to rebuild this file
Implement the functions as described, keeping the cache file name and the atomic write.

## Tests
`backend/tests/test_app_settings.py` covers `model_status` and review.
